# Master Signal Table

Maintained by the Orchestrator agent (weekly, Fridays). Status: NEW / UPDATED / UNCHANGED / **SECURED** / **LOST**.
Every row carries a **Type** that routes it to ONE lane: `net_new_contest | incumbent_renewal | owned_asset | lost | threat_macro`.
- **net_new_contest** → the **opportunity** lane (the only thing shown as a "near-term opportunity"): a winnable, **net-new** deal Printec does **not** already hold and has **not** lost. An incumbency *anchor* in the text (Printec already serves the bank on something adjacent) does **not** by itself make a net-new contest an "owned" or "renewal" row.
- **owned_asset** (e.g. Cashflex, Printec owns/operates it) and **incumbent_renewal** (Printec is the entrenched/sole incumbent and the deal is effectively a renewal/follow-on of held scope, e.g. Pošta Slovenije, Bank of Cyprus) → the **Installed base — own & defend** lane: certain/defendable revenue, **NOT a contest to win**.
- **lost** → the **Lost / competitive-intel** lane: a scope a **named competitor** has won or holds the valuable part of (e.g. Banka Slovenije's sorter maintenance to Giesecke+Devrient, HNB's security estate to INsig2).
- **threat_macro** → context (a macro driver or competitor threat, not a discrete Printec deal).
The engine **excludes** owned_asset / incumbent_renewal / lost / threat_macro from opportunity value, the opportunity rankings and "Top opportunities"; they are kept with their own labels in their own lanes.

**Last triangulation:** 2026-08-31 (sixth full orchestrator run; previous 2026-08-03). All six collector agents filed fresh files this cycle — the widest collection the system has run — producing **1,520 raw finding rows** (A1 616 across 42 banks, A2 263 across 15 procurement portals, A3 141 across 11 regulation workstreams, A4 91 across 7 non-EU markets, A5 178 across 9 markets, A6 220 across 16 competitors). Triage was sharded **by country** across **19 concurrent subagents** — 17 markets plus one footprint-wide regulation shard and one cross-country competitor shard — each seeing every agent's rows for its market so one event seen from several sides became one row. The shards returned 334 candidate rows; the Orchestrator's cross-shard reduce collapsed **29** of them (six Addiko rows into two, six digital-euro rows into one, six ECB AI-cyber rows into one, three Geldservice Austria rows into one, and the euro-redesign, ISO 20022, Asseco/KAL, Brink's, Payten, Euronet and Western-Balkans-TIPS clusters into their best single row), leaving **307 active signals** (previous cycle: 129). **Agent 8 (Futurist) was NOT re-run** and still carries its 2026-07-15 file — see Coverage status.
**Confidence rule:** High requires 2+ *independent agents* (different evidence types — a bank disclosure, a tender notice, a regulator statistic, a job posting, a vendor's earnings) confirming the same bank/theme. Two subagents of the SAME agent are not independent. Single-agent findings cap at Medium. Each row traces to a dated, linked source in an agent's findings file.

## How to read confidence here

A row is **High** only when two or more agents working from different evidence types independently point at the same need. That cross-check is what the Orchestrator adds on top of each agent's own Medium-capped work. **Opp. size** (XL ≥~€5m/footprint-wide programme · L ~€1–5m · M ~€0.2–1m · S <~€0.2m · Unscoped = threat/macro/too-early) and **Type** are **factual context only**. The dashboard does **NOT** estimate Printec's chance of winning a deal — that is the sales teams' judgement, not market intelligence's. Opportunities are ordered **newest development first**; deal size and evidence-confidence are tiebreaks/context, never combined into any win or expected-value score.

Roughly 16 of BiH's 21-22 licensed banks are therefore still outside the scheme (A1, A3, A4, A5). Two things moved materially this cycle. First, a full read of the CBBiH rulebook found Article 7(2), a rolling trigger the master row missed. Any bank that exceeds 500,000 combined real-time-gross-settlement and giro-clearing transactions in a calendar year must become a participant from 1 July of the following year. The addressable set therefore widens every year rather than closing on 01/01/2027 (A3). Second, Article 15 tightens the engineering limits well beyond what the master row recorded. The maximum execution time for an instant payment is 5 seconds, with a 7-second scheme timeout and a 10-second hard timeout. Fraud and sanctions screening must therefore finish inside roughly five seconds, not ten (A3). Article 13 still makes a mobile or electronic-banking app the only permitted way to start a payment. It caps a single order at BAM 5,000, and reserves QR-code initiation to a CBBiH specification that has still not been published (A3, A4). The underlying platform is independently confirmed as Banca d'Italia's TIPS Clone. It went live 20/07/2026 with BiH and Montenegro as the first two central banks on board. | **UPDATED** | Bosnia & Herzegovina — SEPA accession + ISO 20022 structured-address remediation | Bosnia & Herzegovina | The application is now actually filed. On **06/08/2026 CBBiH formally submitted BiH's application to join the Single Euro Payments Area**. This closes a two-year programme run through the SEPA Accession Coordination Board. CBBiH chairs that board alongside both entity finance ministries, both banking agencies and the BiH Banking Association. A draft had been lodged 12/12/2025. The last precondition fell on 28/07/2026, when the FBiH House of Representatives adopted the harmonised financial laws that the Republika Srpska National Assembly had already passed (A1, A4). The European Payments Council is now reviewing the file. CBBiH says clearly that commercial banks must align their IT and business systems with SEPA standards and join the relevant European payment schemes. It also says that a significant part of that work can only be done after formal admission. It expects the first SEPA transactions at the earliest six months after admission. The sales trigger is therefore the six-month post-admission clock, not the application (A1, A4). The World Bank estimates BiH fee savings of around EUR 100m, and CBBiH notes BiH does over 80% of its foreign trade with SEPA countries (A4). Two domestic message-format facts were confirmed this cycle from primary gazette and central-bank text. CBBiH's giro-clearing system already uses the SEPA message format conforming to ISO 20022. It also conforms to whichever European Payments Council rulebook version the central bank designates as current. The 14-15/11/2026 SWIFT SR2026 removal of unstructured postal addresses therefore reaches BiH retail clearing the moment that designation carries it, and that designation is not publicly dated (A3). Meanwhile BiH high-value RTGS is still legally fixed to SWIFT MT formats: MT102, MT103, MT202 and MT205, with mandatory service code BAP. The Governor can set the switch to ISO 20022 pacs.008 and pacs.009 on only fifteen days' written notice once all participants are ready. That is the shortest lead time to a live cutover anywhere in the footprint (A3). | [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [CBBiH — "CBBiH zvanično aplicirala za pristupanje SEPA području"](https://www.cbbh.ba/press/ShowNews/1808?lang=bs) | 06/08/2026 — CBBiH files the official SEPA application, EPC review under way · **14-15/11/2026 SWIFT SR2026 structured-address cut, inherited domestically the moment CBBiH designates a 2025-or-later EPC rulebook** · RTGS ISO 20022 cutover undated, 15 days' notice | A 21-bank migration to IBAN, ISO 20022, credit transfers and direct debits has moved from lobbying to execution. | **NEW** | FBiH Banking Agency — binding ICT-risk decision with an annual external ICT audit due 31/03/2027 | Bosnia & Herzegovina | BiH banks are regulated even where the wider economy is not, and the rulebook now has a hard filing date. FBA's binding "Odluka o upravljanju informaciono-komunikacionim sistemom i IKT rizikom u banci" was adopted 25/02/2025 and has been in application since 31/12/2025. It is BiH's equivalent of the EU's operational-resilience regime. It requires measures to protect the cryptographic keys that encrypt data at rest and in transit. It also requires ICT incident and cyber-threat reporting to FBA, resilience testing, oversight of third parties, and both internal and external ICT audit. The external ICT-system audit report is a standalone report that every bank must deliver to FBA no later than 31 March of each year. **The next one is due 31/03/2027 and applies to all 13 FBiH banks** (A4). On top of that, FBA published its supervisory expectations for 2026 on 20/02/2026. They require penetration testing and red-team exercises, layered security controls, data encryption, network segmentation, continuous monitoring and automated attack response. They also require continuity plans covering rebuilding systems from zero, and a full register of every outsourced activity with direct board accountability. They further require transaction-monitoring systems tuned to actual BiH client behaviour, including cash flows, diaspora remittances and cross-border payments (A1, A4). Banks are already acting. Three of the largest FBiH banks resolved at their spring-2026 AGMs to commission external audits. UniCredit Bank d.d. Mostar appointed KPMG for a financial-statement audit including an assessment of AML obligations, plus a separate information-system audit. ASA Banka resolved to select an external ICT auditor. NLB Banka d.d. Sarajevo appointed an auditor across three separate scopes covering financial statements, the AML segment and the ICT system. Those three banks hold 447 of the Federation's 1,400 ATMs and 15,085 of its 28,834 POS terminals (A1). | [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [FBA — Supervizorska očekivanja u vezi sa postupanjem banaka u 2026. godini](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/1supervizorska_ocekivanja_u_vezi_sa_postupanjem_banaka_u_2026_godini_jzR.pdf) | **31/03/2027 — statutory deadline for every FBiH bank to file its external ICT-system audit report with FBA**, recurring annually · 30/06/2026 three large banks confirm AGM-mandated ICT and AML audits · 31/12/2025 the ICT-risk decision entered into application | This is a named, auditable compliance lane across all 13 Federation banks, and the Republika Srpska banks face a parallel ABRS rule. | **UPDATED** | Bulgaria — Verification of Payee cliff at 01/01/2027 (legal basis contested) | Bulgaria | The contested legal basis is now resolved, and the ATM estate is explicitly in scope. The open verification debt was closed this cycle against the Official Journal text itself. Regulation (EU) No 260/2012 Article 16(9), inserted by Article 1(5) of the Instant Payments Regulation (EU) 2024/886, covers Member States that adopt the euro before 09/04/2027. Their payment service providers must comply with Articles 5a, 5b and 5c within one year of euro introduction. Bulgaria adopted the euro on 01/01/2026, so the duty applies from **01/01/2027**. This is directly applicable EU law, not a regulator's claim, and the previously feared 09/01/2027 non-euro date does not apply here (A3). BNB's own SEPA FAQ, re-read 27/08/2026, gives the same date for instant euro sending and for Verification of Payee (VoP). VoP is the check that the payee name matches the account, and it applies at every PSP licensed in Bulgaria (A3). The decisive new detail for Printec sits in recital 11 of Regulation 2024/886. It names the initiation channels expressly: "online banking, a mobile application, an automated teller machine, a self-service terminal, in a branch or by phone". It requires no difference between instant and other credit transfers across channels. ZVERB paragraph 1 item 16 defines a Bulgarian ATM as a device that also executes transfers between payment accounts. So the ATM and kiosk estate is inside VoP scope as a matter of primary EU text, not inference (A3). UBB went live with VoP on 15/07/2026 with four match outcomes, 24/7, stating the same 01/01/2027 market obligation (A1). BORICA's VoP service has run live since October 2025 and is certified by the European Payments Council as a Qualified Routing and Verification Mechanism (A2, A6). | [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [Regulation (EU) 2024/886 — Official Journal text, CELEX 32024R0886](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R0886) | 01/01/2027 — every PSP licensed in Bulgaria must offer instant euro sending, price parity and full Verification of Payee on every initiation channel; legal basis confirmed at the OJ text on 27/08/2026, UBB live since 15/07/2026 | The remaining lead time is four months, not seventeen. The material change this cycle is that ATMs and self-service terminals are named in the primary text. That turns a payments-department compliance item into a device-estate item, so any bank that scoped VoP to online and mobile only has a gap on its machines. The sale is VoP and name-matching integration into multivendor ATM software and bank kiosks, so a transfer started at the machine carries the mandatory payee check. Add instant-speed sanctions screening with re-screening, real-time transaction monitoring, and hardware security module (HSM) key capacity for 24/7 volumes. UBB and BORICA are reference points, not prospects. A 01/01/2027 go-live had to be funded in H1-2026, so unfunded work now prices as late-stage remediation. | High — a directly applicable EU regulation with a fixed date, confirmed by the regulator and already being worked to by the market | **High** (A1+A3 — a bank's live service launch plus the Official Journal text and the BNB FAQ) | L | net_new_contest | Ask BNB Payment Supervision which Bulgarian PSPs have declared VoP readiness on non-online channels specifically, and approach those with an ATM or kiosk gap first. Get BORICA's BISERA scheme rules for the Bulgarian VoP routing mechanism. One legal point remains for Printec Legal before any date goes into a contract. It is what "within one year of" 01/01/2026 means. The answer is either 31/12/2026 or 01/01/2027. |

| **NEW** | Bulgaria — European Accessibility Act market surveillance now bites on ATMs and payment terminals | Bulgaria | Bulgaria has transposed the European Accessibility Act as the Law on Accessibility Requirements for Products and Services. It was published in State Gazette issue 31 of 11/04/2025 and came into force on 28/06/2025. The gazette text has been read, and it covers the device estate explicitly. Article 2 names **payment terminals and ATM terminal devices** alongside ticketing and information terminals, and it covers consumer banking services. Article 34(1) makes the Chairman of DAMTN, the metrology and technical surveillance agency, the market-surveillance authority for those products under Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. Article 39 lets him order temporary suspension of supply. He may also prohibit making a product available or putting it into service, or order withdrawal of the product from the market. Article 54(1)(8) makes BNB the control body for consumer banking services. The dated change is in the penalties. A transitional provision halved all Chapter Six penalties for infringements committed up to 01/06/2026. Full rates have applied since that date: BGN 1,000 to 5,000 on individuals, or BGN 5,000 to 25,000 on undertakings, doubling on repeat breach. Transitional rules also cover the installed estate. Self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 may run to the end of their economic life, but no more than 20 years from entry into use. The general service-provider transition ends 28/06/2030. One correction was recorded this cycle. The previously carried 28/06/2027 supervisory milestone applies to emergency-call provisions, not to ATMs or payment terminals. No DAMTN or BNB enforcement action against an ATM or payment terminal had been published as at 27/08/2026 (A3). | [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [Държавен вестник issue 31 of 11/04/2025 — Law on Accessibility Requirements for Products and Services (BG)](https://dv.parliament.bg/DVWeb/showMaterialDV.jsp?idMat=233836) | 01/06/2026 — full-rate penalties in force since the transitional discount expired; general service-provider compliance deadline 28/06/2030 and a 20-year economic-life backstop on terminals in use before 28/06/2025 | There are two distinct levers here, and the fines are the less important one. On the supply side, DAMTN can ban or withdraw a non-compliant ATM or payment-terminal model from the Bulgarian market. So every machine sold there needs a current EU Declaration of Conformity and EN 301 549 accessibility evidence. That is a competitive advantage against older or grey-import terminal stock, rather than a cost. On the demand side, BNB supervises the accessibility of consumer banking services. This reaches the same banks at the same moment as the post-euro recycler and cash-automation programme. One engagement can therefore carry both euro-ready cash handling and an accessible interface. With penalties capped around BGN 50,000, sell the market-withdrawal risk and the bundling, not fine avoidance. | Medium — in force with full-rate penalties, but no enforcement action against a terminal has yet been published and the substantive compliance deadline is 2030 | Medium (A3 single-agent, verified at the gazette text) | Unscoped | threat_macro | Monitor DAMTN's market-surveillance register and BNB supervisory announcements for the first accessibility action against a payment terminal or ATM. Confirm whether DAMTN has published a sectoral inspection plan covering self-service terminals. Make sure conformity and EN 301 549 evidence is ready for every ATM and PIN-entry device model offered in Bulgaria, before it is asked for. |

The banking association HUB commissioned an Ernst & Young study that produced three candidate operating models. The shared MBnet infrastructure covers roughly 1,000 machines across 12 member banks. There are 106 million ATM withdrawals a year, worth EUR 19.24 billion. The central bank had earlier proposed the state Financial Agency FINA as operator, then left implementation to direct agreement between the banks. Confirmed again this cycle: nothing about this will ever appear on the national e-procurement portal or on TED. | **UNCHANGED** | Croatia — European Accessibility Act (NN 89/2025): the harshest fines in the footprint, with the central bank as supervisor of bank services | Croatia | Croatia's transposition of the European Accessibility Act, its version of the EU law in national law, was adopted on 06/06/2025. It was published in the official gazette Narodne novine 89/2025 on 13/06/2025, and entered into force on 28/06/2025. The gazette text has been verified (A3). It covers self-service terminals, including ATMs, payment terminals, ticketing machines and interactive information terminals. Market surveillance of those products sits with the State Inspectorate. Surveillance of consumer banking services sits with the Croatian National Bank and the financial-services supervisor, each within its own remit. The penalties are the highest of the five transpositions checked this cycle. A manufacturer that is a legal person faces EUR 6,630 to EUR 132,720 for placing on the market a product not designed to the accessibility requirements. The same band applies to a service provider that fails to make its service accessible. That is an order of magnitude, about ten times, above Cyprus, Romania and Bulgaria. Service providers have until 28/06/2030. Self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 may run to the end of their economic life, but no more than twenty years from entry into use. An annex example literally requires "fitting a socket and installing software on the ATM to allow headphones to be connected so that on-screen text is reproduced as sound". It also requires text-to-speech, time-out warnings in more than one sense, time extension, contrast, keys that can be told apart by touch, and no need for high force. No enforcement decision against any bank or terminal had been published as at 27/08/2026. | [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [Narodne novine 89/2025, item 1231 — Zakon o zahtjevima za pristupačnost proizvoda i usluga](https://narodne-novine.nn.hr/clanci/sluzbeni/2025_06_89_1231.html) | STANDING: 13/06/2025 — Act published in the official gazette, in force 28/06/2025 · service-provider transition ends 28/06/2030 · no enforcement action published as at 27/08/2026 | Croatia carries the sharpest accessibility enforcement risk in the region. Uniquely, the prudential supervisor of these same banks is also their accessibility supervisor for consumer services. That makes it a board-level issue rather than a facilities one. Named exposure covers every large Croatian bank. The work it creates is specific. It includes ATMs with the audio socket and screen-reader stack the annex literally describes, and accessibility retrofits where the chassis allows. It includes multivendor ATM software, so one compliant accessible interface can run across machines from different manufacturers. It also includes accessible PIN pads with remote software push to merchant estates. Above all it includes an estate audit that sets each machine's twenty-year clock. Budgets are committed in 2028-2029 for a 2030 estate, so the audit and roadmap are what sell now. No enforcement action has been taken so far, and that is the pre-enforcement period in which readiness sells. | In force and unenforced — the estate deadline is 28/06/2030, beyond the twelve-month horizon, so this is a standing driver rather than a live trigger | **Medium** (A3 single-agent) | L | threat_macro | Sell an estate accessibility audit and roadmap now, to establish each machine's remaining economic life against the twenty-year cap. | **NEW** | Czechia — EET 2.0 nationwide fiscal sales-recording mandate from 01/01/2027 | Czechia | The Czech Chamber of Deputies approved the government's sales-recording bill, known as EET 2.0, in third reading on 15/07/2026. It has a firm published timetable. Technical documentation appeared on 05/06/2026. A developer seminar was held in Prague on 23/06/2026. A test environment opened on 01/07/2026. EET 2.0 functions, including creation of cash-register certificates in the tax mailbox, follow from 01/11/2026. A free state app for small traders follows from 01/12/2026. Operation starts with a pilot month from 01/01/2027. Full live operation begins on 01/02/2027. The scheme records only contact payments at the point of sale (cash, cards and QR), and leaves out bank transfers and invoices. Importantly, the Finance Ministry says in its own words that the law brings in no compulsory receipt printing and does not require the purchase of new cash-register equipment. The state will give the smallest traders a free web application. The ministry expects CZK 14.4bn a year in extra revenue. Vendors are already selling against the deadline anyway. Those are sold to the acquirers and independent sales organisations whose existing terminals must be made compliant. There is still a real replacement upsell where merchants choose to modernise anyway. That is exactly the angle a local competitor is already using with free hardware. The deciding factor is therefore the ability to match on remote over-the-air updates, not on box price. | High — the bill passed the Chamber and the tax authority is executing a published technical timetable | Medium (A6) | M | net_new_contest | Confirm the bill passed the Senate and was signed, since only the Chamber stage is evidenced. Then identify which Czech acquirers and independent sales organisations need software compliance across their estates rather than new hardware. That is the buyer list. |

They agreed to cooperate as far as joint inspections and shared inspection results. The data date (A3): the DORA register of ICT contracts must be compiled as at 31/12/2026 as its reference date. Each bank submits it to the CNB on the CNB's own earlier cut-off, typically February or March 2027. | **UPDATED** | Czechia — euro deferred: no ERM II, no CERTIS ISO 20022 migration, no digital koruna | Czechia | What moved: a hard new primary date takes Czechia out of the euro pipeline for the rest of the decade. The CNB's own euro-adoption page states this word for word. The next update of the joint Finance Ministry and CNB Assessment is to be submitted to the Czech government by the end of March 2030. That Assessment is the document in which a target date for joining the euro could be set. The last edition, April 2025, advised the government not to set a target date, noting that Czechia met only two of the four required criteria in 2024. Around that, the European Central Bank and Commission Convergence Reports of 24/06/2026 confirm two findings. None of the five reviewed currencies is in the exchange-rate mechanism, and none of the five countries is legally compatible. The next scheduled assessment is in 2028. Czechia passes on price stability and long-term interest rates, but fails on exchange rate and legal convergence. The CERTIS negative was re-tested by a full-text scan of the CNB's official system description on 27/08/2026. It returned zero occurrences of ISO 20022, confirming there is no published migration. The CNB's Czech-language page also still states word for word that its Bank Board has taken no decision on a Czech central bank digital currency. Existing law does not permit issuance at all. | [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [ČNB — Euro adoption strategic documents](https://www.cnb.cz/en/monetary-policy/euro-adoption/), [ECB — reports on progress towards euro adoption, 24/06/2026](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr260624~ec1dcac037.en.html) | 24/06/2026 — Convergence Reports published, koruna outside the exchange-rate mechanism · context: the next government-level euro Assessment is not due until 31/03/2030 | This row removes three spending assumptions at once, and the March 2030 date makes it stronger than the master version. A competitor selling digital-currency readiness in Czechia is selling against the central bank's own published legal barrier. What remains is the real Czech demand: instant euro payments and payee verification with 2027 deadlines, cash automation, resilience and accessibility. | Certain as a statement of position; the only trigger would be an exchange-rate-mechanism application, which is on no timeline | Medium (A3; the second agent that corroborated this in the master no longer files) | Unscoped | threat_macro | Download the April 2025 Assessment and the December 2025 alignment analyses to confirm the March-2030 wording in the government resolution itself. | **NEW** | Hungary — Act XIV of 2026 ATM decommissioning and relocation freeze | Hungary | Act XIV of 2026 §96(1)-(2) rewrote section 3 of the ATM Act with effect from 14/05/2026. Two agents re-read the consolidated statute word for word this cycle (A3, A5). A credit institution may no longer stop operating any ATM that existed when the Act came into force. The same no-closure rule now covers a branch's cash-payout service. Replacement of the machine is expressly carved out ("ide nem értve az ATM cseréjét"). · A relocation is allowed only in a justified case, and only if an ATM keeps operating in the same settlement or Budapest district. The justified cases listed are moving into a settlement with no ATM at all, evidence from average cash-withdrawal volume data, or the landlord ending the site lease. · Subsection (1b) expects that a like-for-like swap may be impossible at a site. The reason given is "for purely technological or technical reasons — in particular the dimensions of the new ATM and its security requirements". In that case the replacement machine may be installed elsewhere in the same settlement. Breach carries an MNB fine of HUF 2m–200m. A1 records the same amendment from OTP's side, and notes that OTP still cut its Hungarian estate by 58 machines in H1-2026. | [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [Act XVIII of 2025, consolidated text in force from 14/05/2026](https://njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2025-18-00-00) | 14/05/2026 — the decommissioning and relocation freeze enters into force, and every Hungarian ATM refresh decision from that date runs through these rules | Hungary has legislated its ATM estate into a guaranteed replacement market. Roughly 5,700 machines nationally can only be swapped, never retired. That total is commonly cited, but the independent validator notes it is not reconciled to any per-bank census in this cycle's evidence. · The statute itself expects the replacement machine may be physically bigger and carry higher security requirements than the one it replaces. That is exactly what happens when an old through-the-wall dispenser is swapped for a deeper deposit or recycling machine, or one with accessibility hardware. A shrinking fleet therefore becomes a multi-year refresh pipeline. · It also adds two attached sales. The first is a chargeable site-survey and fit study for machines that will not fit their old holes. The second is withdrawal-volume telemetry, because a bank now needs volume evidence to justify any move. | High — the law is in force and binds every refresh decision already being taken | **High** (A3+A5, corroborated by A1) | XL | net_new_contest | Take the replacement pipeline to each of the nine banks separately from the 1,039 rural sites. Lead with recycler-class upgrades plus a paid site-survey and fit study against subsection (1b). Attach withdrawal-volume telemetry as the evidence a bank needs to justify a relocation. · Obtain Act XIV §96 from the Magyar Közlöny, together with its explanatory memorandum. Ask MNB whether a replacement that fails the (1b) test needs prior notification. |

| **NEW** | Hungary — 2026-27 payments-infrastructure deadline stack: the VIBER address gap and the instant-euro build | Hungary | Two dated obligations reach the same nine Hungarian banks within fifteen months, and one of them has a verified gap specific to Hungary. The first is the change to postal address data. The European Payments Council's guidance EPC153-22 v2.1 sets 15/11/2026 as a cut-off date. From then, an unstructured postal address is no longer allowed in the SEPA scheme rulebooks and "will hence lead to rejects". This applies to the inter-bank leg and to corporate file upload. The same weekend carries the SWIFT standards release. Germany's Bundesbank separately confirms the removal of unstructured postal address data from the European RTGS system's messages. Production deployment is on 14/11/2026, and the real hard stop is the end of release testing on 28/10/2026. Against that, A3 downloaded and text-extracted the MNB's currently effective business terms and their annexes. It found no occurrences of "ISO 20022", "strukturált cím" or "hibrid" anywhere in the effective annex set, including annexes updated as recently as 03/08/2026. Hungary's domestic real-time gross settlement system VIBER runs ISO 20022 messages, but it has no structured or hybrid postal-address rule and no date, eleven weeks before the international cutover. The second obligation is the instant-euro calendar for non-euro EU states, re-read from the Regulation itself and corrected this cycle. On 09/01/2027 Hungarian banks must be able to receive instant euro credit transfers. They must also price instant transfers no higher than equivalent non-instant ones, with payee-verification services free of charge. On 09/04/2027 the same receiving duty reaches electronic-money and payment institutions. On 09/07/2027 all non-euro payment service providers must send instant euro and provide Verification of Payee, the payee-name-to-account match. Two reliefs exist. There is a carve-out until 09/06/2028 for national-currency accounts, and a right to ask the MNB for permission to cap sending outside business hours (A3). | [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [MNB Üzleti feltételek, 2. melléklet benyújtási rend](https://www.mnb.hu/letoltes/2-melleklet-benyujtasi-rend-20251027.pdf) | 15/11/2026 — unstructured postal addresses stop being accepted across the SEPA schemes, with the international testing hard stop on 28/10/2026 and no matching Hungarian domestic rule in force · 09/01/2027 Hungarian banks must receive instant euro transfers and meet charge parity · 09/07/2027 sending plus Verification of Payee | Hungarian banks will run two address regimes at the same time across the same customer base. Structured or hybrid formats apply to SEPA and correspondent traffic from mid-November, while free text is still allowed at home. That dual-regime problem is the commercial opening. It calls for dual-format handling, and for monitoring of rejects and rejection messages at cutover. It also calls for sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening re-tuned to the structured town and country fields. Customer-data cleansing then has to satisfy the international leg without breaking the domestic one. The instant-payments step is a re-scope rather than a new product. Payee verification has to reach the self-service and kiosk channel as well as the core. The January step is close enough that any bank still scoping it is already late. The conclusion is to sell remediation and managed services on the address leg, because the budget-commit window for it has closed. In parallel, scope the July-2027 sending and payee-verification step now. | High — both are fixed, directly applicable dates, and the Hungarian domestic gap was verified at annex level rather than inferred | Medium (A3 only) | M | net_new_contest | Watch the MNB's consultation page for proposed amendments to its business-terms annexes before 15/11/2026. A Hungarian hybrid-address rule would appear there first. Ask each Hungarian bank whether its payee-verification scope covers domestic forint and non-account-number identifiers, since that gap is the follow-on opportunity. Check whether the MNB has published any policy on the outside-business-hours sending permission or the national-currency-account carve-out. |

| **UPDATED** | Kosovo — POS whitespace + deposit-ATM upgrade (BPB Printec-incumbent) | Kosovo | The market numbers changed sharply this cycle. The central bank's August-2026 card report, with data to 31/12/2025, shows card-accepting POS terminals reaching about 30,300, up from 20,913 a year earlier. That is a 45% jump of roughly 9,400 terminals deployed in a single twelve-month period, and the largest single movement in Kosovo's payment infrastructure (A1, A4). The ATM picture went the other way. The fleet grew only 8% to 686 machines, of which just 394 can accept a cash deposit and only 57 can start a credit transfer. Because banks added dispensers faster than deposit-capable machines, the deposit-capable share fell from 59.4% to 57.4%. The cash-in gap therefore widened to 292 machines that cannot take a deposit and 629 that cannot make a transfer (A1). The commercial case is now quantified. ATM deposits carry 32.1% of all card-transaction value on those 394 machines, while POS payments carry only 17.8%. The highest-value work in the country is done by the smallest and least-equipped part of the estate. Monthly data to June 2026 show both flows still speeding up. ATM deposit counts are up 14.0% year-on-year and ATM withdrawals up 10.5%, while POS payments are up 47.0% (A4). Terminals offering cash-back at the till rose from 18 to 245 in one year, an early sign of merchant-based cash-out replacing ATMs. | [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [CBK — Përdorimi i kartelave në Kosovë, August 2026 edition](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Perdorimi-i-kartelave-ne-Kosove.pdf) | 14/08/2026 — the central bank published its August-2026 card-usage report with 2025 device counts; monthly Bulletin No. 298 of 07/08/2026 extends the series to June 2026 | There are two separate, independently sized openings. First, a 45% one-year expansion of the acceptance estate creates demand for terminal supply, estate management, encryption-key injection and terminal-management software at real scale, and it is happening now. A fleet installed in one burst starts its refresh clock together. Second, 292 dispenser-only ATMs in a euro-using, cash-heavy economy form a countable and widening upgrade pipeline for cash recyclers. A recycler re-dispenses the notes customers deposited, so cash-in-transit runs and vault cash both fall. Add to that ATM application software to bring transfer and bill-payment functions to the 92% of machines that lack them. | High — both series published and still accelerating in H1-2026 | **High** (A1+A4) | XL | net_new_contest | Ask the central bank's Payment Systems Department (payment.systems@bqk-kos.org) for the per-bank breakdown of the 686 / 394 / 57 split, which the public report withholds. That one table turns a market-level gap into a named target list. Separately, ask each acquirer who supplied the ~9,400 net-new 2025 terminals. Also ask when that fleet's first refresh and terminal-management renewal falls. |
| **UPDATED** | Kosovo — KIPS upgrade and instant-payment bank-side integration across all banks | Kosovo | The programme moved from planning into live operation this cycle. Banca d'Italia confirmed that the shared TIPS Clone instant-payment platform officially went live on 20/07/2026. The platform is a standalone copy of the European Central Bank's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement system, built for the Western Balkans. The central banks of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro were the first to join. A second onboarding window is scheduled for November 2026, when the central banks of Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia are expected to join (A3, A4). The platform settles in participating countries' own currencies in central bank money, and in euro in commercial bank money. That dual-money model has separate screening and reconciliation consequences. Kosovo's central bank has now bought both pieces it needed. The connectivity layer was awarded to Nexi (see the separate Nexi row). A ten-month advisory contract for design and programme management was awarded to Paylume SRL of Brussels at EUR 295,000 on 22/07/2026, from exactly one expression of interest (A2). The central bank's Annual Report 2025 names the four overlay schemes being scoped on top of the national system: QR Code, Request to Pay, Proxy ID and Verification of Payee. It records that during 2025 it signed an agreement with the European Payments Council for use of the SCT, SDD and SCT Inst schemes (A4). At sector level, the Banking Association's payments committee chair has stated commercial banks' full commitment to join. The central bank's own invited expert described the work as "elimination of existing technical gaps" (A3, A5). No commercial-bank connection date has been published anywhere. | [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [Banca d'Italia — TIPS Clone platform for instant payments in the Western Balkans goes live](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/) | 20/07/2026 — the shared instant-payment platform went live regionally; November 2026 is the scheduled onboarding window for Kosovo's central bank; the Paylume advisory contract awarded 22/07/2026 runs to about May 2027 | The central rail is bought and dated, so the remaining money is on the bank side. Every Kosovo commercial bank must connect to the national system, map ISO 20022 payment messages, offer instant payments through mobile and internet banking, and reconcile a rail that never closes. The banks are Raiffeisen, NLB, TEB, ProCredit, BKT, Banka Ekonomike and Banka për Biznes. Round-the-clock irrevocable settlement removes the overnight batch window in which fraud used to be caught. That pulls through real-time transaction monitoring, instant sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening, hardware security modules and 24/7 managed operations. The four named overlays, QR, Request to Pay, Proxy ID and Verification of Payee, are the merchant-acceptance and channel work that follows. | High for the platform and the window; Medium for Kosovo specifically, since Banca d'Italia says "expected to join" rather than committed, and Kosovo's Payment Services law is still unpromulgated | **High** (A2+A3+A4; A5 corroborates) | L | net_new_contest | Get in front of the central bank's Payment Systems Department (director Lumni Rrustolli) and the Banking Association payments committee (chair Akile Cernobregu Hashani) before the November window. | **NEW** | Kosovo — CBK Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management (Kosovo's DORA) | Kosovo | Kosovo's version of the EU's digital operational resilience rules is now binding, and the compliance date has already passed. The central bank's board approved the regulation on 29/08/2025, and it came into force on 15/09/2025. Article 67 required financial institutions to comply from 01/06/2026. It is a rulebook of roughly 50 pages. It covers governance, ICT asset and information management, and management of third-party service providers. It also covers budget forecasting, project management and IT acquisition, secure development, testing, patch deployment, access rights and cloud services (A3, A4). It goes further than the EU minimum on incident timing. Article 31(10) requires the central bank to be told no later than four hours after an incident is discovered. An interim report follows within 72 hours, and a final report within 30 days. The reporting template asks for the hardware manufacturer, the software developer, and the make and model of the affected applications and the systems they run on. The template explicitly names ATMs ("bankomatet") alongside SWIFT, RTGS and ACH as critical systems whose compromise must be declared (A4). Commercially, the most important clause is Article 10. Institutions must set aside enough budget for cyber preparedness. Article 10 also states that "the cybersecurity budget should be independent of the FI's overall ICT budget". The stated purpose is "to ensure that business-related systems developments do not compete for resources allocated to protecting ICT systems" (A3). | [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [CBK — Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management (English, PDF)](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/ENG-Rregullore-per-sistemet-e-informacionit-1-1.pdf?lang=en) | 01/06/2026 — the compliance obligation took effect for every Kosovo financial institution; supervisory examination, not preparation, is now the live conversation | Every Kosovo bank is non-compliant today if it cannot show an ICT asset register, a third-party provider register, a documented patch process and a four-hour incident pipeline. The reporting template names ATMs as regulated critical infrastructure and asks for make, model and firmware evidence. That turns directly into demand for ATM and device telemetry and monitoring, multi-vendor estate visibility software, and managed field services for documented patching. It also creates demand for auditable encryption key management, remote key injection and real-time transaction monitoring. The ring-fenced cybersecurity budget in Article 10 is the most commercially useful clause in the market. It forces a spending line the board can see, and ordinary business projects are not allowed to draw on it. Kosovo has no firm SEPA date, so this regulation, rather than payments, is the near-term spend trigger. | High — binding since 01/06/2026 and supervisory enforcement is the next step | **High** (A3+A4) | M | net_new_contest | Offer every Kosovo bank a gap assessment against this regulation. Build it on device telemetry and an ICT asset register that produces the four-hour incident evidence. Lead the commercial conversation with the Article 10 ring-fenced budget. Ask the central bank's supervision department whether on-site inspections have begun, and how it plans to check ATM-estate compliance. |

| **NEW** | Kosovo — Law 08/L-304 on Banks compliance deadline, with the Payment Services law still blocking SEPA | Kosovo | Law No. 08/L-304 on Banks, adopted 05/12/2024, was promulgated by presidential decree of 20/01/2026. It was published in Official Gazette No. 2 of 27/01/2026 and entered into force about 11/02/2026. Article 147(1) gives banks and branches of foreign banks that held a licence at entry into force twelve months to comply. That is a statutory date of about 11/02/2027, with three years for foreign bank branches on certain provisions. Article 1(2) states the law is harmonised with the EU capital requirements regulation and directive, and with the bank recovery and resolution directive. That leaves only the Payment Services law 08/L-328 and the AML/CFT law 08/L-333 stuck in constitutional review. The central bank spells out the consequence in its own annual report, word for word. The restrictions from non-promulgation "prevented the final application to SEPA and, consequently, resulted in the loss of the opportunity to keep pace with neighbouring countries". A replacement route is already moving. The Government approved a new Draft Law on Payment Services at its 8th meeting, by Decision No. 08/08 of 03/04/2026, and it is heading to the Assembly. The same blockage holds back a second opportunity. The central bank's Regulation on access of non-bank payment service providers to payment systems, adopted 25/11/2025, lets non-bank providers open settlement accounts directly in the national system. Each bank has to fix regulatory reporting, data quality and risk systems. That means core and channel integration, regulatory reporting and data quality work, anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer screening, and managed services. It also removes one of the three blockers to Kosovo's SEPA application, which shortens the runway once the remaining two clear. Kosovo is the one Western Balkan market where the SEPA compliance wave is held back rather than already spent. Two independent release valves now exist: a court ruling, or Assembly passage of the replacement draft. Either would trigger a compressed multi-bank remediation programme. Behind that sits a new buyer class of e-money institutions, payment institutions and fintechs. | **NEW** | Kosovo — cash-operations compliance spine: the ECB tested-machine gate and the new Counterfeit Monitoring System | Kosovo | Kosovo's Regulation on Cash Operations was board-approved 27/12/2023 and has been in force since 01/02/2024. It was obtained and read in full this cycle, and it is stronger than previously understood. Article 5(4) covers the processing machines that financial institutions use to check the authenticity and fitness of euro banknotes and coins. Such a machine may only be put into use if the Eurosystem has successfully tested it. Article 5(5) requires banknote machines in use or planned to appear on the European Central Bank's published list of tested machines. Coin machines must appear on the European Commission's equivalent list. Articles 17(3) and 18(3) explicitly extend the same requirement to machines operated by the customer. Article 22 copies the ECB machine taxonomy in full, covering cash-in, cash-recycling and combined cash-in and cash-out machines, with recyclers required to check both authenticity and fitness. The regulation also bars anyone from providing cash deposit or withdrawal services through customer-operated machines without a central-bank licence, or from importing or holding such machines. A linked implementation plan of 12/02/2024 commits the central bank to "the deployment of several ATMs and other devices enabling the electronic payments (POS), or financial self-services". This applies in Serb-majority municipalities, including the four northern ones (A1). New this cycle, on 15/07/2026 the central bank announced it had begun EU-supported work to set up a Kosovo Counterfeit Monitoring System. Only the headline and date are verified, because the site sits behind a Cloudflare gate and no archive copy exists (A1). The volume behind all this is large. About 20.65 million euro banknotes, 33.23% of everything banks deposited in 2025, were classified unfit and withdrawn. | **NEW** | Montenegro — instant payments live at all 11 banks: Verification of Payee mandate, irrevocable rail, 5-cent fee cap | Montenegro | On 20/07/2026 the Central Bank of Montenegro put the TIPS Clone instant-payment platform into production. It is a national settlement system cloned from the European Central Bank's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement service. It was built with Banca d'Italia and financed by an EUR 8m World Bank credit. Banca d'Italia confirms that Montenegro and Bosnia were the first two central banks to join. Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia are expected in a second window in November 2026 (A3). · Uniquely in the region, the whole sector went live at once. The regulator publishes customer video guides from all eleven banks: Addiko, Adriatic, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, Lovćen, NLB, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Zapad banka and Ziraat. It states plainly that all 11 banks are IPS participants (A1, A4). · Three things follow for the banks. First, the enabling amendments to the Law on Payment Transactions make Verification of Payee compulsory, in line with EU Regulation 2024/886. Before confirming an order, the bank must check that the payee name matches the IBAN, warn the customer on a mismatch, and do this free of charge. Fines for non-compliance are EUR 10,000-40,000. Funds must reach the payee within ten seconds or be returned without delay (A6). · Second, the rail is irrevocable. The regulator's own FAQ says instant payments as a rule cannot be recalled. Two days after go-live, the central bank had to warn the public about a phishing wave impersonating itself and Western Union with a fake EUR 50 giveaway link. This is the typical pattern for authorised-push-payment fraud, where the victim is tricked into sending the money themselves (A4). · Third, a Council Decision of 17/07/2026 caps the fee on a domestic instant transfer of up to EUR 200 made by mobile or internet banking. The cap is five euro-cents on both the sending and the receiving side, against a previous average of 32 cents. The regulator estimates EUR 1m of annual savings, rising to EUR 2.8m (A1, A4). · First official volumes were 56,678 instant transfers worth EUR 21.53m in the 12 days of July, at an average ticket of EUR 380 and full availability. The regulator's directorate head reports that volume rose five-fold from launch day to end-July. He also reports that only "a little over 60%" of credit transfers are currently initiated electronically (A4, A5). | [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [CBCG — Instant plaćanja (TIPS Clone)](https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/instant-placanja-tips-clone) | 20/07/2026 — TIPS Clone go-live across all 11 banks · 17/07/2026 Council Decision capping the fee at 5 cents · 22/07/2026 central-bank phishing warning · 13/08/2026 first official IPS volumes published · monthly statistics continue, August figures due mid-September 2026 | Every Montenegrin bank now carries the same three obligations at the same moment. It removes fee income on small payments, so a bank can only protect its margin by cutting its cost to serve. | **NEW** | Romania — instant euro payments: banks must receive by 09/01/2027 and send with Verification of Payee by 09/07/2027 | Romania | The timetable is now settled at the Official Journal text, after two cycles of conflicting corrections. Under Regulation (EU) No 260/2012 Art. 5a(8), as inserted by Regulation (EU) 2024/886, payment service providers (PSPs) in non-euro Member States face two dates. They must offer receiving of instant euro credit transfers by 09/01/2027. They must offer sending by 09/07/2027. The 09/04/2027 date applies only to electronic-money and payment institutions, not to banks. The 09/01/2027 date also brings charges parity, so an instant transfer may cost no more than the equivalent non-instant one. 09/07/2027 brings mandatory Verification of Payee, the check that the payee name matches the IBAN (A3). Romania has already legislated. On 12/02/2026 the Government adopted an emergency ordinance amending Law 231/2015. It requires providers to settle within a maximum of 10 seconds, regardless of day or hour. It requires the service through all payment-initiation channels used by clients, and mandatory Verification of Payee. It also adds a duty the baseline missed: periodic reporting of fee levels and the percentage of rejected transactions to the European authorities. The ordinance also gives payment and e-money institutions access to designated payment systems. The ordinance number could not be confirmed, and "OUG 5/2026" must not be cited (A3). Salt Bank ran the first local implementation of instant euro over TRANSFOND's RO-TIPS on 14/01/2026. It was built in about three months with TRANSFOND and Montran. Montran's own boilerplate in that release claims anti-fraud and QR products alongside instant payments, so it competes for the fraud layer too (A3, A6). Montran also holds BNR's ReGIS and SaFIR maintenance. It supplied the central RoPay and instant-payments solution behind UniCredit's 02/02/2026 go-live. Ten banks are live on RoPay, with BRCI still in implementation (A6). | [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [Regulation (EU) 2024/886 amending Reg. 260/2012, Arts. 5a(8), 5b(3), 5c(9)](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R0886) | 09/01/2027 — Romanian banks must receive instant euro credit transfers and meet charges parity; 09/07/2027 — sending plus mandatory Verification of Payee | The first hard date is roughly four months away. The budget for it is therefore either already committed, or the bank is late. The commit window for the 09/07/2027 sending and Verification-of-Payee step is now, from Q3-2026 to Q1-2027. The expensive words in the Romanian ordinance are "all payment-initiation channels". Internet banking, mobile, branch and file-based corporate channels each need instant payment plus name-matching. The new rejected-transaction and fee reporting duty is a straightforward transaction-monitoring and regulatory-reporting requirement. The sellable layer is what Montran does not claim. That includes instant sanctions and AML screening, deep transaction monitoring and HSM key capacity. It also includes Verification-of-Payee name-matching tuning, channel work and managed cut-over. The ATM and kiosk side matters too, where the free-amount bill and instant rails meet. Expect to displace existing suppliers rather than simply add to them. The size of the remediation market is not established. The circulating figure that "only four or five of about thirty Romanian PSPs are live" has no source and must not be used. | High — these are fixed, directly applicable EU dates with national implementing law already adopted | **High** (A3+A6) | L | net_new_contest | Get the ordinance from Monitorul Oficial. | **NEW** | Romania — DORA and AML supervisory evidence is becoming the gate on Printec's own managed-services sales | Romania | Two supervisory cycles now bear on whether Printec can be bought, rather than on what it sells. The first is the DORA Register of Information. 31/12/2026 is the reference date, not the deadline. Financial entities file to their national supervisor on that supervisor's own earlier cut-off, typically in February or March 2027. The supervisor then forwards the filing to the European supervisory authorities by 31/03/2027. The authorities do not publish the national cut-offs, so BNR must be watched separately. Only subcontractors that effectively underpin ICT services supporting critical or important functions are reportable (A3). The second is threat-led penetration testing, a controlled attack by hired testers, under DORA Articles 26-27. It is specified by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1190. That regulation covers scope, method, internal testers, remediation phases and supervisory cooperation for mutual recognition. Scope is set at entity level and covers critical functions end to end. For a retail bank, that pulls in the ATM channel, the acquiring and terminal estate and the monitoring layer (A3). The Romanian hook is explicit. Banca Transilvania's H1-2026 risk narrative names growing dependency on third-party providers and outsourced services as a board-level risk, amid a persistent cyber threat landscape. At the same time, the bank has pulled software development in-house (A1). Alongside these, AMLA's provisional list of entities for direct supervision is expected at the end of September 2026. National supervisors submitted their input by 15/08/2026. Harmonised AML sanction standards are heading to the Commission for adoption ahead of the 10/07/2027 application date (A3). | [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [EBA — FAQ on reporting of registers of information under DORA](https://www.eba.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2025-03/31bb6e60-7d10-4405-a8c5-9f04934630ac/20250328%20-%20DORA%20RoI%20reporting%20FAQ%20(updated).pdf) | 31/12/2026 — reference date for the Register of Information; Romanian banks file to BNR on its own earlier cut-off, expected Feb–Mar 2027, and BNR forwards by 31/03/2027 | This is a sales-readiness cost rather than a bank capex line, and it cuts both ways. Gazette 43/2026): 6- and 12-month adaptation deadlines | Serbia | The 21-page official decision was read in full this cycle, so the detail is now confirmed. NBS Executive Board decision no. 14 of **07/05/2026** was published in Službeni glasnik RS 43/2026. It enters into force on the eighth day after publication, and it fully repeals the 2019/2020/2021 regime (A1, A3). · Point 33 sets two transition periods for institutions already running video identification. They must align their business and internal acts **within six months** of entry into force. They must adapt their **technical solutions within one year** (A1). · Point 30 adds a requirement the master row missed. Any institution planning to offer video identification must notify NBS **at least 30 days before starting**. It must submit internal acts, proof of staff training, and the list of document-issuing states its staff are trained on. It must also submit evidence of premises, and a full description and prior assessment of the technical solution. Before that period ends, it must give NBS staff a **live real-time demonstration of the entire process for every customer category** (A1). · The decision creates two modes. In the direct mode, an employee takes part in a live call. In the indirect mode, supervision and verification can happen before the relationship begins. In exceptional cases they can happen within 72 hours afterwards, under enhanced monitoring and transaction limits (A1). · The demand pattern has changed, and this is the most material change this cycle. NBS Q2-2026 data show 168,733 distance contracts concluded electronically, up 25.9% year on year. Of these, **129,728 were fully electronic (+40.6%), but only 39,005 used video identification — down 6.5% year on year, the first fall on record**. In the 2025 base year, video identification was the faster-growing leg at +75.4% (A4). | **UPDATED** | Serbia — SEPA / instant-payments wave | Serbia | The regulator has now confirmed the shape of this precisely, and it is narrower than the master row assumed. NBS's own FAQ, re-read 27/08/2026, states that Serbia became the 41st SEPA member on **22/05/2025**. It also states that **18 of 19 banks** went live on SEPA Credit Transfer on 4 and 5 May 2026. · Serbian banks are only in the initial phase. All of them take part as **indirect** participants, routing through correspondent parents abroad, and **there is still no Serbian date for SEPA Instant Credit Transfer** (A3). Raiffeisen's own explainer confirms the mechanics from the bank side. It is credit transfer only, with no 24/7 operation. It runs on working-day cycles with settlement no later than next day, and a 13:00 cut-off set by its Austrian parent (A1, A5). · OTP's customer article is blunter still. Euro payments from Serbia to SEPA banks remain international payment traffic, executed under clearer rules rather than as domestic SEPA payments (A1). · There is a new competitive fact. **ASEE announced on 16/06/2026 that it completed SEPA implementation for 14 Serbian banks, all going live on the same day**. It combined its own gateway platform with changes inside the banks' core systems (A6). · The forward-looking evidence is now in the central bank's own procurement plan v9 of 26/08/2026. That plan carries **accession to SEPA and TIPS**, and a payment-systems software upgrade to link NBS infrastructure to the EU's (A4). NBS separately plans an **ISO 20022 migration in 2026** of the Serbia–Bosnia–Montenegro FX clearing platform. That platform is a nameable set of 20 banks plus three central banks, which currently exchange SWIFT MT messages (A4). · Meanwhile the domestic instant rail keeps growing on its own. There were 34,459,117 instant transactions in Q2-2026, up 30.7% year on year and worth RSD 442bn. July 2026 alone carried 11.3m payments at a one-second average execution time, with three banks carrying about 64% of value (A4). Serbia is aligning to PSD2, not PSD3, and three draft laws went to consultation in late May and early June 2026 (A3). | [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [NBS — SEPA u Republici Srbiji: najčešća pitanja i odgovori](https://www.nbs.rs/sr/scripts/showcontent/index.html?id=21465&konverzija=no) | 26/08/2026 — NBS 2026 procurement plan v9 adopted carrying SEPA/TIPS accession and the payment-systems software upgrade · 16/06/2026 ASEE delivered SEPA for 14 Serbian banks in one same-day go-live · SEPA credit transfer live since 05/05/2026, **no instant-payment date exists** | The work that can be bought in Serbia over the next 12 to 18 months is the move from indirect to direct scheme participation. | **UPDATED** | Serbia — cash-in, not cash-out, is where the ATM channel is growing | Serbia | The Q2-2026 regulator series, published 19/08/2026, moves every number in the master row and strengthens the argument. · The national estate reached **3,412 ATMs and 195,121 POS terminals at 30/06/2026**. That is up from 3,336 ATMs and 187,957 POS terminals at Q1-2026, and from 3,196 and 177,185 a year earlier. The year-on-year change is **+216 ATMs (+6.8%) and +17,936 POS (+10.1%)**. Add 6,278 virtual points of sale (+21.4%) and 13.7m cards issued to 7.1m users (A1, A4, A5). That +6.8% is **the highest year-on-year ATM growth in the whole published NBS series back to Q1-2016** (A4). · Deposits are moving faster than withdrawals. **ATM cash-deposit transactions reached 3,406,129 worth RSD 173.9bn in Q2-2026, up 31.9% by count and 53.6% by value year on year. Withdrawals grew just 4.5% by count and 15.7% by value.** Deposit value is now 31.5% of withdrawal value, up from 23.7% a year earlier. Deposits are 11% of ATM transactions by count, but 24% by value (A1, A4, A5). Cash withdrawal at the branch teller **fell 3.9%** (A5). · On the wider cash series, deposit value has run at 1.4 to 1.5 times withdrawal value since 2024. In H1-2026 withdrawal value was flat year on year at +0.4%, while withdrawal count fell 5.8%. So cash out is no longer growing even in nominal terms, while cash in still is (A4). Card purchases at Serbian merchants hit 237.9m in Q2-2026, up 19.3% year on year and more than double the Q2-2022 figure (A1, A4). · The branch base is going the other way. NBS told the press in May 2026 that bank organisational units fell from 1,558 in March 2021 to **1,288 in March 2026**. That is a cut of 17.3%, with sector headcount down to 21,732 (A4). Bank-level disclosures confirm the same shift independently. Some 86% of Banca Intesa's dinar deposits and 97% of Raiffeisen's Premium-segment cash transactions already happen on machines (A1). | [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [NBS — Acceptance network statistics (prihvatna_mreza.xlsx)](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/platni-sistem/statistika/el_novac/prihvatna_mreza.xlsx), [NBS — Payment transactions in the acceptance network (trans_prihvatna_mreza.xlsx)](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/platni-sistem/statistika/el_novac/trans_prihvatna_mreza.xlsx) | 19/08/2026 — both NBS workbooks updated with Q2-2026, superseding the Q1-2026 figures of 3,336 ATMs and 187,957 POS · 26/08/2026 NBS press release on card growth · next quarterly refresh expected ~November 2026 | This is the single set of numbers that supports every Serbian self-service proposal, and it should be the first slide in all of them. The claim is now stronger. Serbia is one of the very few European markets adding ATMs, at the fastest rate in a decade. A near one-to-one deposit-to-withdrawal ratio is exactly the condition where recycling beats separate deposit and dispense machines. Recycling machines re-use deposited notes, which starts to cut cash-in-transit journeys and vault holdings. The ATM upturn is only three or four quarters old, so present it as a trend rather than a guarantee. Ask the NBS Payment System Department whether deposit and recycling-capable ATMs can be broken out on request. | **UPDATED** | Slovakia — eKasa cashless mandate + deposit-ATM expansion | Slovakia | The legal duty to let customers pay cashlessly on any sale above EUR 1 is live, and the legal detail is now pinned down in the primary text. Act 384/2025 Z. z. took effect 01/01/2026. Its section 15(1) acceptance duty applied from 01/05/2026, after Act 30/2026 Z. z. postponed it from 01/03/2026 (A1, A2). · Four points are new this cycle. First, section 15(3) expressly allows a third party to supply the technical means that confirm a QR-code payment back to the cash register. That is an explicit legal opening for a private vendor to run the payment-confirmation layer. Publishing the technical specification is a legal duty, and the Financial Directorate had still not done so at 27/08/2026. · Second, the penalty ladder is far harder than previously reported. A first detection brings a formal instruction only. A second carries EUR 500-15,000, and each further detection EUR 3,000-40,000. Sections 17(5)-(6) class it a "particularly serious breach" that can cost the merchant its trade licence. · Third, on the Financial Directorate register of valid certifications at 19/08/2026, Printec Slovakia holds decision 322095/2025 for "Printec eKasa Service verzia 1.2", effective to at most 20/06/2030. The register carries 65 decisions across 38 companies, so certification is a qualifier to compete rather than a differentiator. Diebold Nixdorf holds two of its own decisions, and also supplies the protected data store into a third party's certified stack. · Fourth, the regulator confirms two recurring merchant-side replacement cycles. eKasa credentials expire every 2 years. The protected data store fills up and must be swapped every 2-6 years. The 5-year certification clock binds only the manufacturer, and must not be sold to merchants as a forced replacement. · The QR-code alternative means the smallest merchants can comply with no hardware. That caps terminal upside and favours SoftPOS. The reported jump from 70,943 to 77,711 POS terminals could not be verified this cycle, and must not be quoted. | [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [Slov-lex — zákon č. 384/2025 Z. z. §§15-17, consolidated 28/02/2026](https://www.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2025/384/20260228.html), [FR SR register of valid eKasa certifications at 19/08/2026](https://www.financnasprava.sk/_img/pfsedit/Dokumenty_PFS/Podnikatelia/eKasa/2026/2026.08.20_Cert_eKASA.pdf) | 27/08/2026 — FR SR eKasa portal and certification register re-read; mandate live since 01/05/2026; Printec certification valid to at most 20/06/2030 | This is the largest single POS and acquiring trigger in Slovakia. Art. 18(5) lets a contracting authority amend **live** tender documents to apply the new rule where the deadline has not passed (A3). Carried forward and still valid: NLB Group's Annual Report 2025 states that 58 ATMs in Slovenia support voice-guided transactions for blind and partially sighted customers. | **UNCHANGED** | Slovenia — commercial banks sit outside public procurement, so the pipeline is invisible to tender monitoring | Slovenia | This is a structural negative finding, confirmed again this cycle over a wider period. Portal sweeps re-run on 27/08/2026 show the following results. The automatic-banknote-dispensing-machine classification and all its sub-codes have zero notices since 01/01/2024. Coin-handling machines also have zero notices since 01/01/2024. Sorting and banknote-handling equipment has six notices since 2024, but all of them are Pošta Slovenije parcel and letter sorters, and none is a banknote sorter. Counterfeit detection has six notices, all of them the tax authority's desktop counters, with no bank at all. A title search for "bankomat" returns two notices in the portal's entire history. Both come from a 2019 municipality paying towards the running costs of rural ATMs. So the only ATM procurement Slovenia has ever published is a town paying to keep village machines running, and never a bank buying a machine. The reason is legal. | **UPDATED** | Slovenia — MONEYVAL enhanced follow-up meets NLB's "AI at scale: AML" | Slovenia | The core of the master row still stands. MONEYVAL published Slovenia's 6th-round mutual evaluation on 07/07/2026 and placed the country in enhanced follow-up. It found moderate improvement in risk assessment, but significant remaining gaps on terrorism financing, held back by structural data gaps. What changed this cycle is the EU layer and the hiring evidence. AMLA's 2027 selection timeline is now dated from primary sources. National supervisors, including Banka Slovenije, had to send data to AMLA by 15/08/2026. The provisional list of eligible obliged entities is expected to be final at end-September 2026. The first selection process must start by 1 July 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2024/1620, and must finish within six months. Direct supervision then follows from 2028. To be eligible, a group must operate in at least six Member States including its home state, which catches the cross-border groups active in Slovenia. On transposition, the Commission's monitoring page as at 07/08/2026 records Slovenia as having communicated full measures for the 10/07/2025 tranche. The fixed general deadline is 10/07/2027. The beneficial-ownership and bank-account-register articles were due 10/07/2026 (A3). Separately, the Slovenian market is clearly hiring for exactly the skill the evaluators say is missing. Addiko Slovenia was running three data roles at once: data engineer, data governance analyst and data analyst. It was also running two group market and liquidity risk roles. Delavska hranilnica posted a data-governance specialist on 25/08/2026 (A5). Carried forward and still valid, NLB's own technology deck names "AI at scale: AML, retail credit risk, chatbots" as a board-level programme. | [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [AMLA — next step toward 2027 selection for direct supervision](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en), [European Commission — AMLD6 transposition monitoring](https://finance.ec.europa.eu/regulation-and-supervision/financial-services-legislation/enforcement-and-infringements-banking-and-finance-law/monitoring-banking-and-finance-directives/anti-money-laundering-and-terrorist-financing-directive-vi_en) | 15/08/2026 — national supervisors' AMLA data submission fell due · **provisional list of directly supervised entities expected end-September 2026** · first AMLA selection must commence by **01/07/2027** · MONEYVAL enhanced follow-up opened 07/07/2026 | The named weakness in Slovenia is data: the quality of risk assessment, complete customer and beneficial-owner records, and the ability to prove a risk-based approach.
