| **UPDATED** | NBU Resolution No. 67 — mandatory one-time-password identity capture at self-service cash-in terminals | Ukraine | This resolution was re-checked line by line against the official 9-page NBU PDF this cycle, and is now sized against the exact device count. Resolution No. 67 of 16/06/2026 was officially published on 18/06/2026. It came into force on 26/06/2026. New clause 124-2 applies to every cash-in at a self-service payment kiosk, whatever the amount. It requires the payer to key their full mobile number on the kiosk screen. The provider or its commercial agent must then check that the payer owns that number, using a one-time password sent by SMS or read out by phone call. The payer keys that password on the kiosk screen. Clause 124-3 obliges the provider, including where commercial agents are used, to take continuous steps to make it impossible or less risky to pass the password to someone else. That includes shortening how long the password is valid. Clause 124-4 has a much longer list of exemptions than first reported. It covers budget payments, meaning taxes, fines and administrative-service fees. It covers utilities under the Housing-Services Law, plus fixed telephony, TV, internet and security. It covers rail tickets including suburban, urban and suburban transport fares including e-tickets, route passenger transport, and transport-card top-ups. It also covers mobile-service payments within the provider up to UAH 500 per month per number, and cash-in to top up an account with an issued payment instrument. The resolution also sets cash-handling rules for the new financial-inclusion bank licence type and its commercial agents (A4). On scope, there were 22,953 PTKS kiosks at 01/07/2026. Each one needs a screen-flow change plus SMS or voice one-time-password integration (A4). | [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [NBU Постанова № 67 of 16/06/2026](https://bank.gov.ua/admin_uploads/law/16062026_67.pdf?v=19) | 26/06/2026 — in force; a non-compliant terminal may not execute the cash-in at all. Re-verified against the official PDF and sized at 22,953 kiosks as at 01/07/2026 | Every cash-in kiosk in Ukraine needs a new screen flow, an SMS or voice one-time-password integration, and a remote roll-out across a fleet that cannot be visited machine by machine. That is a terminal-management job rather than a site visit. Clause 124-3 makes the risk of password-sharing, which is money-mule activity, a standing legal duty. It is therefore a rules-and-monitoring requirement rather than a one-off interface patch. The broad exemption list cuts both ways. Operators will want conditional branching rather than one blanket prompt, which means more integration work, not less. | In force since 26/06/2026 — the remediation demand is immediate, and the ban on executing the payment makes non-compliance an outage rather than a project | **Medium** (A4 this cycle; the A3 regulatory read that corroborated it last cycle was not repeated) | M | net_new_contest | Ask EasyPay, iBox and City24 directly how they built the one-time-password step and the exemption branching, and whether the NBU has started enforcing it. The independent operators are the ones most likely to be short of capacity. Approach banks on the receipt-retention and monitoring feed, not only on the terminal interface. Combine the pitch with the UAH 2,000 note reconfiguration, since both land on the same 22,953 kiosks in the same quarter. |
| **UPDATED** | NBU Resolution No. 81 — customer verification methods widened for financial inclusion | Ukraine | The master row's headline needs correcting. Two agents separately re-checked Resolution No. 81 of 15/07/2026 against the NBU's own notice of 16/07/2026 and the official legal portal. Neither found the geolocation, geotagging, photo-metadata-timestamp or no-editing requirements that the master row leads with (A3, A4). What is confirmed is different and narrower. The resolution amends the Regulation on banks' financial monitoring, which is Regulation No. 65 of 19/05/2020, and it came into force on 17/07/2026. First, it allows the original identity document to be presented during verification by a third party, meaning an accompanying or authorised person. That document may also be handled by the verifying bank employee where the client cannot present it alone. Second, it allows the client's consent to a photo to be shown by audio or video recording, where a handwritten or electronic signature is impossible. Separately, under the financial-inclusion law, the new financial-inclusion bank licence type may use a commercial agent. That agent may establish the beneficiary of a transaction, and carry out identification and verification under the same regulation. The NBU adopted the surrounding rules for this type of institution in June 2026 (A3, A4). The master row's other elements were not re-confirmed this cycle and should be treated as unverified. Those elements are acceptance of the Diia e-passport and the electronic taxpayer card including QR versions, and replacing "authorised employee" with "authorised bank employee or qualified electronic seal". | [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [NBU — verification methods widened, 16/07/2026](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/news/all/rozshireno-perelik-sposobiv-verifikatsiyi-bankami-kliyentiv-dlya-tsiley-finansovoyi-inklyuziyi) | 17/07/2026 — in force; compliance required now. The financial-inclusion bank package was adopted in June 2026 and the first licences are the forward trigger | Ukraine has made agent-assisted and third-party-assisted verification legal, with consent captured on audio or video. That is a real fit for a digital-onboarding and e-signature stack: video identification, audio and video consent capture, and qualified timestamping. It can be delivered through tablets and kiosks at agent points rather than in branches. Most importantly, it creates a new kind of buyer that has never bought branch technology. That buyer is the agent networks, post offices and retailers acting for a financial-inclusion bank, which need an onboarding device and eKYC software instead of a branch. The master row's remediation-buy framing rested on the geotag claim, and it does not survive this cycle's re-reading. | In force since 17/07/2026; agent-based and financial-inclusion-bank onboarding scales through 2026–2027 as licences are issued | **High** (A3+A4) | M | net_new_contest | Get the consolidated text of Regulation No. 65 as amended, and map the capture and consent requirements to the Namirial video-KYC flow. Do not brief the geotag or unedited-photo requirement until it is found in the amended annex text. Two agents looked for it this cycle and neither found it. Track the first financial-inclusion bank licences, and who supplies their agent-onboarding stack. Clear any biometric or photo-capture design with Printec's DPO before pitching. |
| **NEW** | NBU — AML enforcement biting at named banks, plus a published 2026 inspection calendar and an outsourcing-friendly monitoring rule | Ukraine | Three strands come together into the clearest dated compliance trigger in this market. **(1) Fines, published 07/08/2026** for July enforcement against 2 banks and 19 non-bank institutions: **JSC Raiffeisen Bank fined UAH 16,100,000** for poor customer due diligence (checks on who customers are), not using a risk-based approach and risk-reduction measures, not managing risks from new and existing information products, business practices or technologies (including those that allow transactions without direct customer contact), late reporting of threshold transactions, and not giving the NBU complete information. It also received a written warning covering missing enhanced measures on politically exposed persons, **failure to configure and automate generation of the standard response forms in Annex 1 to Regulation No. 90**, not updating customer questionnaires within 10 working days, and not passing on all received payer information on transfers. **JSC Bank Ukrainskyi Kapital fined UAH 42,545,000** in total, including the same automation failure and being unable to give data to inspectors on time (A3, A4). **(2) A named, dated inspection calendar**: the NBU's plan, revised 31/07/2026 and updated 25/08/2026, lists Q1 Bank Ukrainskyi Kapital, Q2 Cominbank and UkrSibbank, Q3 Sky Bank and EPB, **Q4-2026 Asvio Bank, CB Globus and Bank KD**. The chain is already proven: the Q1 bank was fined in July (A3). **(3) A draft resolution on payment-service-provider control over payment operations** (consultation opened 17/07/2026, closed 14/08/2026, comments published 21/08/2026) sets single standard approaches to monitoring and reconciling payment operations, and **explicitly allows third parties to perform parts of the monitoring function**. | **NEW** | NBU Resolution No. 85 — TrekSEP payment-tracking duties, one-hour SLA already live | Ukraine | This is a dated payments-tracking rule that is already binding, rather than a future deadline. NBU Board Resolution No. 85 of 05/08/2026 was officially published 06/08/2026. It amends the Instruction on interbank payment operations in the national currency, which is Resolution No. 16 of 03/03/2023. It defines the TrekSEP message and service, a support service that lets users track the stages of a SEP payment. It also defines the concept of a SEP instant-transfer participant. New point 46-4 applies to every SEP participant. It must send the payment-execution status to the SEP central processor as soon as possible, and no later than one hour after that status is set. This covers the status set in the participant's own automation system, and in the system of any non-bank provider settling through an account with that participant. New point 46-5 obliges the participant to let the user check payment status remotely by sending a TrekSEP message. It must also return the execution-stage information to the user through the remote channel. A critical correction is confirmed from the legal text. Point 4 of the resolution delays only paragraphs five to seven of sub-point 3 of point 1, that is point 46-5 and its two sub-points only, to 01/01/2027. Everything else, including the one-hour status-push duty in point 46-4, took effect the day after publication, on 07/08/2026 (A3, A5). For context, SEP carries over 99% of Ukrainian interbank payments. It is a designated systemically important RTGS, or real-time settlement system, running 24/7 on ISO 20022 since 01/04/2023. It averages 1.5m payments a day worth about UAH 778bn. It has offered instant credit transfer within 10 seconds since 01/12/2024, and SEP-4.2 with multi-currency support is being developed. | **NEW** | NBU Resolutions No. 70, 72 and 73 — third-party risk management now binding on banks and payment providers | Ukraine | Three NBU Board Resolutions introduce third-party risk management, which means managing the risks that come from outside suppliers. All three are dated 30/06/2026 and all took effect on 01/07/2026. Resolution No. 70 covers banks and banking groups, and amends the Regulation on the organisation of the risk-management system. Resolution No. 72 covers financial payment service providers, and Resolution No. 73 covers insurers. The NBU's own notice confirms the requirements. Institutions must identify, assess, control, monitor and reduce third-party risks. They must **assess counterparties in advance, covering financial condition, business reputation and operational capability**. Contracts must meet minimum requirements, and provider compliance must be monitored on an ongoing basis. Institutions must also set out the actions to take when a provider, or a critical provider, falls short. Business-continuity management must take third-party risk into account, and termination and exit plans are required. Institutions must set criteria for when a third-party relationship creates critical risk to continuity or to clients. The NBU says institutions have "sufficient time" to review existing supplier contracts, but it publishes no transition date. The stated legal basis is Basel Committee recommendations, the payment services directive and Solvency II. It is not the IMF memorandum, PSD2 Article 20 or an EBA consultation paper, which were the basis assumed before. One further point was verified separately. NBU Resolution No. 143 of 09/12/2025, on organising information-security and cyber-protection measures by financial service providers, exists and came into force on 13/12/2025. The widely quoted "13/12/2026 transition end" could not be confirmed and is not stated on the NBU legislation page (A3). This regime applies directly to Printec's own supplier contracts, and it also creates new demand. | [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [NBU — third-party risk management requirements established](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/news/all/ustanovleno-vimogi-schodo-upravlinnya-rizikom-tretih-storin-dlya-bankiv-nadavachiv-platijnih-poslug-ta-strahovikiv) | 01/07/2026 — in force for banks, payment service providers and insurers; contract re-papering is live now with no published transition deadline | Every Ukrainian bank must now list, pre-assess and continuously monitor each critical technology supplier. That includes ATM and recycler vendors and outsourced field-service providers. Banks must also hold written exit plans. This has two effects for Printec. It raises the due-diligence standard an existing supplier has to meet, so Printec's Ukrainian contracts need checking against the critical-contract criteria. It also creates budgeted demand in three areas. The first is auditable device telemetry, which means remote data from the devices themselves. The second is monitoring, managed and field services backed by service level agreements. The third is documented continuity and exit evidence. Ukrgasbank has already started writing this same compliance-grade wrapper into its ATM service contracts. | High — already in force since 01/07/2026, and re-papering of existing supplier contracts is under way | **Medium** (A3 single agent) | M | net_new_contest | Get the text of Resolution No. 70 from zakon.rada.gov.ua, because the SSL handshake to that host failed this run. | **UPDATED** | Ukraine — flat ATM fleet against 96% cashless and continuing branch contraction | Ukraine | The structural case is now backed by exact counts from the NBU's own data file, and the single most useful number has finally been published. PC_table_1.xlsx at 01/07/2026 records 15,768 ATMs. Only 2,785 of them, or **17.7%**, can take deposits. That share has been flat since 2024: 2,624 at 01/01/2024, then 2,754, 2,727 and 2,785. Self-service payment kiosks, known as PTKS, grew 68% in a single year on a smooth monthly path. They rose from 13,310 at 01/01/2025 to 22,376 at 01/01/2026. By 01/07/2026 they reached 22,953. Trade POS terminals reached 582,547, up 4.3% in six months, and card-accepting points reached 699,258, up 13.9%. SoftPOS tap-to-phone devices grew 65% to 69,783, and POS with cash-out reached 319,345 (A4). Cashless payments are 96% of card transactions by count, but only 67% by value. So roughly UAH 1.27tn still came out of the cash channel in H1-2026, across about 196m withdrawals. There are 153.2m cards issued, but only 61.1m are active, or 40%. That is down from 65.4m in January, as state support programmes ended. 21.1m cards (34.5%) are tokenised. About 99% of in-store cashless transactions are contactless, by both count and value (A1, A4). Cash itself is not shrinking. Currency in circulation rose from UAH 759,753m at 01/01/2025 to 866,943m at 01/01/2026. It then reached 921,808m at 01/08/2026, a rise of 14.1% in 2025 and a further 6.3% in seven months (A4). Branches continue to close. There were 4,754 operating structural units at 01/07/2026, down 38 in the quarter and down 5.1% since 01/01/2025. A further 787 are temporarily suspended: Oschadbank 640, Raiffeisen 52 and PrivatBank 2 (A1, A4). Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine shows the steepest reduction. It had 256 business outlets at 30/06/2026 against 295 a year earlier, a fall of 13.2% and the largest cut in RBI outside Russia. Over the same period its customers rose 8.2% to 3.124m (A1). ## Coverage status this cycle (completeness gate)

Most-recent dated file per source folder (as of 2026-08-31):
- 01-bank-disclosures **2026-08-27** ✓ (42 banks targeted, 42 returned, 616 signals) · 02-tenders **2026-08-27** ✓ (15 portals, 263) · 03-regulation **2026-08-27** ✓ (11 workstreams, 141) · 04-statistics **2026-08-31** ✓ (7 non-EU countries, 91; EU counts scripted) · 05-jobs **2026-08-31** ✓ (9 markets, 178) · 06-vendors **2026-08-31** ✓ (16 competitors, 220) · **08-futurist 2026-07-15 ⚠ NOT re-run this cycle — six weeks stale.**
- **No collector emitted a `⚠ COVERAGE WARNING` this cycle.** Agent 4's run was interrupted by a usage limit on 27/08 (all 7 country agents died after checkpointing, and that harness pass returned 0 signals with a 7-country warning), but it resumed from the per-unit checkpoints and **completed on 31/08 with 7/7 countries covered, 0 empty units**. The collection window for A4 is therefore 27–31 August 2026.
- **Structural coverage limit, not a miss:** Agent 4 researches only the 7 non-EU markets by design (EU counts come from the scripted `fetch_ecb.py`), so **Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Hungary, Romania and Slovenia have no researched country-statistics rows this cycle** — their national figures arrived press-tier or via Agent 1. This caps confidence on several rows in those markets and is why the Czech national ATM count rests on a vendor's blog.
- **Two markets recovered from last cycle's blackout.** Montenegro and North Macedonia were recorded as "returned nothing" on 2026-08-03. Both are now covered from local-language primary sources — Montenegro with 26 wholly market-specific rows including a bottom-up nine-bank fleet reconciliation (~641 locations against the regulator's 664), North Macedonia with ~48. **Cause of the earlier blank identified:** NBRSM's web estate is Cloudflare-gated and yields only to a real browser session — A1 reported it wholly inaccessible while A4 defeated it and pulled cell-level data.
- **Kosovo is monitorable after all.** The prior cycle's claim that it cannot be watched without an e-prokurimi economic-operator account was not tested this cycle, and two account-free channels are confirmed: BQK publishes cancellations, awards, prices and losing bids as open PDFs, and World Bank STEP under P507881 is a second route.
- **Access blockers still live:** the EPC site (Cloudflare, blocking five scheme dates) and NBRSM without a browser session. Albania's procurement portal remains login-only.
